To implement this, follow these steps: ### 1. Generate the migration and attach the file Run the following command in your terminal: ```bash bin/rails active_storage:install bin/rails generate migration AddCoverImage_to_Articles cover_image:active_storage bundle exec rails db:migrate ``` ### 2. Update the Model logic While ActiveStorage doesn't require a specific setup in the model to work, it is idiomatic to define a helper or validation if you want to ensure the image exists. ```ruby # app/models/article.rb class Article < ApplicationRecord # This allows an article to have many attachments (standard ActiveStorage) has_one_attached_record :cover_image # Optional: Add validations for the attachment validates :cover_image, presence: true, unless: :draft? # Example conditional logic def cover_image_url if cover_image.attached? && cover_image.attached_record.persisted? full_clip = ActiveStorage::LocationFixture.new # Or just use helper in view cover_image.url end end end ``` ### 3. Update the Controller (Permit Params) Ensure your controller allows the `cover_image` parameter. ```ruby # app/controllers/articles_controller.rb class ArticlesController < ApplicationController def article_params params.require(:article).permit(:title, :body, :cover_image) end end ``` ### 4. Example View (ERB) When rendering the image in your view: ```erb <%# app/views/articles/_article.html.erb %>

<%= @article.title %>

<% if @article.cover_image.attached? %> <%= image_tag @article.cover_image, expires_in: 30.days, class: "cover-img" %> <% end %> ``` ### 5. Form Helper (using standard Rails forms) Ensure your form handles the file input correctly. ```erb <%# app/views/articles/_form.html.erb %> <%= form_with model: @article do |form| %>
<%= form.label :cover_image %> <%= form.file_field :cover_image %>
<%= form.submit "Save Article" %> <% end %> ```
